summary.value: The North Holland Blue is a heavy Dutch meat chicken bred around Purmerend, north of Amsterdam, in about 1900. Farmers crossed Belgian Malines birds with hardier local hens to feed the city's demand for white chicken meat. After World War Two faster American meat breeds pushed it aside, and the last big farm closed in 1977. It comes in one color, cuckoo, and males are paler than females. Dutch birds have clean legs, while the British standard asks for lightly feathered shanks. Roosters weigh about 7.5 to 9 pounds and hens about 6 to 7 pounds. Hens lay roughly 180 to 240 tinted eggs a year. The breed is quiet and docile, grows quickly, and is valued for firm, high quality meat. Hens crossed with suitable males give sex-linked chicks, and a bantam form exists.
